alt: Individual identity, what makes a person distinctive, set against collective identity, belonging to a group, with three features: identities are socially constructed, relational, and multiple and changing.
caption: Identities are built socially, defined against others and always shifting.

alt: A grid of the seven bases of identity, age, gender, ethnicity, class, religion, disability and nationality, each with its key idea and useful sociology such as Mannheim, Butler, Fanon, Savage, Oliver, Anderson and Billig.
caption: For each basis, say how it is constructed and how it changes.

alt: Connell’s hegemonic masculinity, Mac an Ghaill’s crisis of masculinity among young working-class men, and diversifying femininities with persisting pressures over appearance and care.
caption: Gender identities have widened, but dominant ideals and pressures persist.

alt: Two overlapping circles, heritage culture and culture of settlement, with hybrid identity in the overlap. Cards summarise Hall’s view of diaspora identity as becoming and Robin Cohen’s types of diaspora.
caption: Hybrid identities combine cultures and keep being reworked.

alt: Goffman’s impression management, with users performing a front-stage self and finding support in online communities, set against Zuboff’s argument that platforms harvest data and shape identities for profit.
caption: Users perform identities online, but inside systems built for profit.

alt: Bauman, Giddens and postmodernists see identity becoming chosen through consumption and globalisation; structural sociologists argue class, gender, ethnicity, disability and money still constrain it. A plan applies this to whether class still matters.
caption: Identities feel chosen, but structures and money limit the choices.
